citation_policy: Numeric refs are this study's ledger IDs; original web_search result ids are preserved per entry.

sources.title: From the CEO: What's coming to YouTube in 2026 (Neal Mohan)
sources.used_for: Every format on every screen; long-form, Shorts, music, livestreams, podcasts; Shorts averages 200B daily views; YouTube #1 in US streaming watchtime nearly 3 years (Nielsen); 93% of US 18-27 year olds and 79% of US teachers say YouTube helps learning (2025 Kantar / Oxford Economics); creators as new studios; $100B paid to creators in 4 years.

sources.title: Connect with creators on the biggest screen (Made On YouTube 2026)
sources.used_for: Over half of YouTube's top 100 creators have TV as their most watched interface; Shorts series / seasons / episodes; microdramas surpassed 6.5B views in H1 2026 with watch time +50% YoY and TV views +90% YoY; 300M users engage with posts daily.

sources.title: Measure key moments for audience retention - YouTube Help
sources.used_for: Intro = % still watching after first 30s; spikes = moments rewatched or shared; dips = skipped/abandoned; flat = watched start to finish; typical retention compares 10 latest videos of similar length; retention data takes 1-2 days; key moments need video >=60s and >=100 views.

sources.title: Understand your YouTube engagement - YouTube Help
sources.used_for: Engagement tab snapshot: watch time (hours), average view duration, views; audience retention report.

sources.title: Understand your YouTube content performance - YouTube Help
sources.used_for: Impressions, impressions CTR, views, average view duration, average percentage viewed, engaged views, unique viewers, regular viewers.

sources.title: Videos: list - YouTube Data API v3
sources.used_for: chart=mostPopular returns most popular videos for a content region and video category; part=snippet,statistics returns categoryId, title, viewCount, likeCount; quota cost 1 unit; up to 50 IDs per call.

sources.title: Search: list - YouTube Data API v3
sources.used_for: Keyword search; 100 calls per day in the Search Queries quota bucket (1 unit in that bucket); default 25 results; type=video, order, publishedAfter, videoDuration filters exist.

sources.title: VideoCategories: list - YouTube Data API v3
sources.used_for: Returns categories associable with videos; regionCode makes the list region-specific; quota cost 1 unit.

sources.title: Qualified watch hours and Shorts views (YPP) - YouTube Blog
sources.used_for: Qualified watch hours come from public long-form videos including podcasts and archived livestreams; Shorts watch hours do NOT count as qualified long-form watch hours.

sources.title: List of most-viewed YouTube videos - Wikipedia
sources.used_for: Top 30 most-viewed are children's songs, music videos and one advertisement; Baby Shark Dance 17.28B; since Bad Romance (2010) every #1 most-viewed video has been a music video; page self-describes as a dynamic list that may never satisfy completeness.

sources.title: NASA Brand Center - Images and Media
sources.used_for: Acknowledge NASA as source; no implied endorsement; insignia / identifiable-person restrictions.

sources.title: NASA Strategic Partnerships - Promotional Content
sources.used_for: Exact wording: 'Short-form social media content generally is considered promotional content' and 'Imagery with ... current astronauts ... may not be used in promotional content'; NASA cannot endorse or appear to endorse; no co-branding/sponsorship.

sources.used_for: Public-interest framing: 'star of Artemis II', Hansen leaning in, face upside down and warped, straw catch, light bending like a glass lens.

sources.title: Watch the Artemis II astronauts have fun with bubbles
sources.used_for: Surface tension forms the sphere; light bends and inverts images; retired astronaut Karen Nyberg's 'what you see depends on how we look' lesson; playful tone.

sources.title: 'Like a crystal clear ball!' NASA water-in-space video
sources.used_for: Jeremy Hansen upside-down through the orb; straw catch and release; 'uniquely human' audience reaction; NASA statement that crew had fun with water in weightlessness.

sources.title: Artemis II water drop footage amazes the network
sources.used_for: Social reactions and a viewer safety question about water near electronics - useful raw material for a myth-vs-fact chapter, NOT a verdict.

sources.title: Artemis II broadcast error used to stoke false 'staged' claims - AFP Fact Check
sources.used_for: A broadcast text-overlay glitch was misused to claim the mission was staged; the glitch clip drew over 1.5M views. Guardrail for the 'why your brain says CGI' chapter: do not amplify or invent conspiracy claims.

sources.title: Astronauts as Influencers - Nautilus
sources.used_for: Artemis II cross-platform exposure: 27.3M TV news viewers for return, 18.1M for launch, 650k splashdown stream, 22M archived video. These are broadcast/stream figures, NOT YouTube views of our clip and NOT a forecast.

sources.title: Tube Trends: longer videos to compete with TV (Tubular Labs data)
sources.used_for: Q1 2026 US creators uploaded 6.6M videos of 20+ minutes, 80.3% at least 30 min; MrBeast 628M long-form views in Q1; 44 creators above 100M views on longer content.

sources.title: 9 YouTube Trends Creators Need to Watch in 2026 - vidIQ
sources.used_for: Long-form viewing on TVs, video podcasts, multi-format channels, stronger title/thumbnail testing, community revenue.

sources.title: Faceless science channels and reusable hooks - FalconVid
sources.used_for: Directional examples of curiosity-gap long-form science titles with reported million-view videos (Nebula Prophecy, GoDocs, OctoLab). Numbers NOT verified by us.

sources.title: Best Science YouTube Channels 2026 - TubeStats
sources.used_for: Directional channel-scale context (Kurzgesagt, Vsauce, Veritasium, NASA). Subscriber/view numbers NOT verified by us.

sources.title: Short-Form Hook Library: 500 viral videos (2026 manual analysis)
sources.used_for: Pattern frequencies in a self-described manual sample: direct claim with specific number 14%, POV 11%, contradictory pattern interrupt 10%, curiosity gap 9%, listicle preamble 7%. NOT an official YouTube statistic.

sources.title: How to Get a YouTube API Key in 2026 - OutlierKit
sources.used_for: API key is free within a 10,000-unit/day default quota; what the Data API cannot do: breakout/outlier detection vs channel baseline, arbitrary-video transcripts, keyword search volume, semantic look-alike channels, derived audience intelligence.
